title: Indra and the mirror
hook: Indra and a demon king learn the self from a pan of water; atman is not the body
carry: the self is not the body

segments.voice: Yesterday, the gods hid from Death inside om, and the Mandukya Upanishad began: om, this syllable is all this.

Another old story. Prajapati, the creator, announced: there is a self that never grows old, never dies, never grieves, never hungers. Whoever finds it wins everything. Two students came to learn it, firewood in hand, the old sign of a student. Indra, king of the gods. And Virochana, king of the demons. They served Prajapati for thirty-two years. Then he said: dress in your finest clothes and look into a pan of water. What do you see? Ourselves, sir, all dressed up, down to our hair and nails. That, said Prajapati, is the self. Both went home happy.
screen: `A SELF THAT NEVER DIES.` → `A PAN OF WATER.` → `THAT IS THE SELF?`

segments.voice: Virochana went home and taught the demons: the body is the self. Dress it, feed it, please it, and you win this world and the next. But Indra, on the road home, stopped. If the body is the self, then when the body is dressed up, the self is dressed up. When the body goes blind, the self goes blind. When the body dies, the self dies. That's no self that never dies. I see no good in this, he said, and turned around. Many teachers read Prajapati's answer as a test: the reflection was the easy answer, and only one student questioned it. That's the teaching, and one of Hinduism's biggest: atman, the self. You have a body, and you are more than it. The Mandukya's second verse says it plainly: all this is Brahman, and this self is Brahman. Ayam atma brahma, one of the four great sayings, the mahavakyas. Then it maps that self in four quarters. The first is vaishvanara, the waking self: knowing outward, enjoying solid things, food, faces, the chair under you. In om, it's the first sound, a. The Mandukya doesn't call waking life fake, or the body bad. Waking is a real quarter. Just not the whole. Today the pan of water is a phone. A person can spend an hour on one photo and feel their worth rise and fall with it. Hindu teaching doesn't say stop caring how you look. It says that face is where you live, not who you are. Indra stopped on the road. Anyone can.
screen: `VIROCHANA: THE BODY IS THE SELF.` · `INDRA TURNS BACK.` · `AYAM ATMA BRAHMA: THIS SELF IS BRAHMAN.` · `THE FIRST QUARTER: WAKING.` · then, large: `MORE THAN THE BODY.`

segments.voice: Be fully in the waking state: your weight on the chair, the sounds around you, the air on your skin, the taste in your mouth. This is the first quarter, knowing outward. Then gently notice that you're aware of all of it, the body included: it's appearing to you. Ask Indra's question quietly, is this all of me, and rest there without answering.
The Mandukya Upanishad. The self is Brahman, and it has four quarters. The first is vaishvanara: the waking state, knowing outward.
Your line: the self is not the body. Indra turned back on the road; tomorrow, what Prajapati told him next.

howItsDone: 'Ayam atma brahma' (Mandukya 2) is taught in Hindu Vedanta as one of four mahavakyas, great sayings, each drawn from a different Veda.
